John the Baptist. A Jewish preacher who baptized people as a sign of repentance and is best known for baptizing Jesus in the River Jordan. He was an ascetic figure who prepared the way for Jesus's ministry, preaching a message of repentance and moral reformation in the Judean wilderness. He was distinctive in his appearance, wearing a coat of camel's hair with a leather belt and eating locusts and wild honey. Baptism became a defining act in early Christian tradition through his practice. He was eventually beheaded by Herod Antipas, the tetrarch of Galilee, after criticizing the king's marriage to his brother's wife. His head was brought to Herod on a platter at a feast, a dramatic moment captured in Christian and secular literature. In Christian theology, he is understood as the forerunner who prepared Israel for Jesus's arrival, and both Christian and Jewish sources recognize him as a significant religious figure of his time.
